kai (infra): Heads up — seeing repeated Xid 48 spikes on a subset of APNE nodes over the last 6 hours, seems tied to small-batch int8 inference jobs.

maya (runtime): Noted. Are these on the quantized embedder pool or general-purpose nodes?

kai (infra): Mostly quant pool (pool-q-apne1). Rough sample of node ids: gpu-az1-12, gpu-az1-15, gpu-az2-03.

jen (serving): We rolled an int8/quantized embedder variant yesterday for a cohort, small-batch traffic shape (~1-4 tokens). Could be related.

diego (sre): Xid 48 historically correlates with memory ECC or pcie faults but often shows up from driver/kernel/firmware races under weird batch shapes. Any ECC counters?

kai (infra): ECC counters are not consistently enabled for persistent collection; ops-bot returned noisy samples. I pulled quick dmesg from gpu-az1-15: 

ops-bot: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (0x48): PID 4321, GPU 0: 00000000:83:00.0
[ 1234.568000] NVRM: Xid 48 detected during context switch
[ 1234.568100] pcieport 0000:81:00.0: AER: Corrected error, type B2, multiple
```

maya (runtime): That PCIe AER line is interesting — suggests transient link errors. But why tied to int8 small-batch? Maybe request pattern creates frequent context switches/KV cache churn triggering a fragile firmware path.

jen (serving): We do have very high QPS with tiny latencies on that cohort. Batching disabled, no KV cache hits.

diego (sre): Hypothesis list: 1) PCIe AER flakiness on a subset of cards 2) driver/firmware mismatch exposed by int8 path 3) model runtime micro-pattern (tiny batches + high async concurrency) stressing DMA.

kai (infra): Proposed immediate actions: 1) Quarantine suspect machines (soft drain) 2) Collect full nvml and AER logs for 24h window 3) Run reproduce job with pinned workload on a single node to see if we can trigger reliably 4) Try driver rollback/upgrade on one host as A/B test.

jen (serving): I can route a small % of the cohort away from pool-q-apne1 and throttle QPS on the rest. Will do a 10% diversion now.

ops-bot: Routing change applied: cohort-q -> pool-q-eu1 (10%) at 3740001450

maya (runtime): For repro I can deploy a reproducer pod that fires tiny requests at 400 rps with no batching. Command to run locally: 

ops-bot: ```
kubectl -n inference run repro-small --image=redwood/repro:latest -- 
  --target http://localhost:8080/v1/generate --qps 400 --batch-size 1 --duration 10m
```

kai (infra): I'll schedule soft-drain on gpu-az1-15 (leave current pods until they finish, don't place new). Drain command: `rackctl drain gpu-az1-15 --soft --reason "xid48-investigation"`

infra-oncall: A note — draining might bump load on neighboring racks; we should watch preemptive autoscale.

diego (sre): While draining, capture: `nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nv_q.xml`, `dmesg -T | grep -i nvrm > /tmp/dmesg_nvrm`, and `journalctl -u kernel | tail -n 500`. Also capture PCIe AER counters: `sudo ethtool -S eth0` (where applicable) and `lspci -vvv`.

maya (runtime): I'll run the reproducer pinned to gpu-az2-03 and stream logs. If flaky reproducer triggers Xid 48 locally, we can test driver 535.86 -> try 535.101 on the A/B host.

jen (serving): Also let's confirm model binary was produced with the correct CUDA/TF Ops for int8 path; I'll checksum the build artifact and post the model config.

kai (infra): ETA for initial data dump: 30m after repro runs. If repro is stable, we'll attempt driver upgrade on gpu-az2-03 at low traffic window (02:00 APNE local).

diego (sre): If driver change doesn't help, next step is to RMA card(s) that consistently repro after isolation. But let's avoid mass replacements without reproducible failures.

maya (runtime): Quick interim mitigation: enable tiny batching window (5ms) for cohort to reduce context-switch pressure — can we try 5ms and see?

jen (serving): I can toggle batching window via feature flag for that cohort. Rolling to 5ms now; will monitor latency tail and error rate.

ops-bot: Feature flag toggle: cohort-q/enable_min_batch_window -> 5ms at 3740001820

kai (infra): Logging plan: create a short-lived dashboard with these panels: Xid count by node, PCIe AER errors, nvml ECC counters, per-node QPS and small-batch ratio. Share link when up.

diego (sre): Agree. Also add model route tag so we can correlate which model variant spikes precede Xid events.

jen (serving): Checksum for model v1.9-qint8: sha256: b3c9f2... (pasted).

maya (runtime): Reproducer started on gpu-az2-03. Streaming logs...

ops-bot: Reproducer logs (snippet): ```
2026-03-20T01:12:45Z request id=abc123 status=200 latency=12ms
2026-03-20T01:14:02Z NVRM: Xid (0x48)  pid=8765 gpu=0
```

kai (infra): Got it. Two repro hits in first 10m. Diego, want me to proceed with driver bump on the A/B host?

diego (sre): Yes. Bump to 535.101 on gpu-az2-03 and monitor for 30m. If Xid stops -> likely driver/firmware timing fix. If not -> collect full PCIe logs and schedule RMA conversation.

ops-bot: Driver upgrade scheduled: gpu-az2-03 -> 535.101 at 3740002000 (ETA now)

maya (runtime): Post-upgrade reproducibility window started.

jen (serving): I'll keep cohort throttled until we have a signal.

kai (infra): If anyone sees sustained ECC counter increases, ping infra-oncall immediately.

infra-oncall: Acknowledged.

diego (sre): Summary / next steps: 1) Monitor A/B host for 30m 2) If clean, slowly scale cohort back and observe 3) If failures persist, prepare RMA plan and expand sampling to more nodes with same firmware.

jen (serving): Thanks team. I'll update the incident doc after 1h with results.

kai (infra): I'll post the dashboard link + collected logs in 40m.

ops-bot: Incident note created: infra-2026-03-20-xid48-apne1-quant.

maya (runtime): Will follow up with reproducer artifacts (perf traces + nvstack) in thread.

diego (sre): Great work. Keeping this thread pinned until resolved. :white_check_mark:
